content:
Apple has cited a recently stayed securities fraud lawsuit to support its request to halt further proceedings in the lower court while its partial legal dispute with Epic Games is being heard by the Supreme Court. Details are as follows.

Apple invoked the ruling to help Judge Rogers decide whether to stay the case.

Earlier this year, a class action lawsuit filed on behalf of the Coral Springs police officers' pension plan accused Apple of securities fraud.

The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled investors into believing that the company had complied with the injunction in the Epic Games case and was on track to deliver its announced AI Siri features as scheduled.

Meanwhile, Apple continues to challenge the civil contempt ruling in the Epic case. The issue before the Supreme Court is that the 2021 injunction required Apple to allow outside payment options but did not explicitly prohibit it from charging commissions on such transactions; the Supreme Court must determine whether the commissions Apple charges on transactions outside the App Store can be ruled as civil contempt of court.

Last week, Apple requested the lower court to stay proceedings to clarify what commissions, if any, the company may collect on transactions outside the App Store while the Supreme Court considers the contempt ruling.

Apple argued that the Supreme Court's ruling would affect proceedings in the lower court, but Epic Games objected to this argument.

In fact, Apple has filed a similar motion to stay proceedings in the Coral Springs securities fraud case, as it also involves the Epic Games case.

Earlier today, Judge Noël Wise granted Apple's motion, meaning the Coral Springs case will remain stayed until the Supreme Court rules on the civil contempt finding.

This ruling prompted Apple to submit Judge Wise's decision in the Epic Games case to Judge Rogers to argue that its motion for Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers to stay proceedings should likewise be granted.

Excerpts from Apple's submission to Judge Rogers:

Judge Rogers is currently weighing Apple's arguments in favor of staying the case against Epic's arguments opposing a stay. Apple hopes Judge Wise's decision will persuade Judge Rogers to reach the same conclusion.

Notably, in its reply opposing Epic's opposition to a stay, Apple also asked Judge Gonzalez Rogers, if she denies the stay motion, to hold the proceedings in abeyance so that the company may seek a continued freeze on the case from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court while the contempt ruling is being separately reviewed by the Supreme Court.
